subject: general
question: If an increase of 40% is observed on an amount in 4 years at simple interest, what will be the compound interest on ₹80,000 after 4 years at the same rate of interest?
solution:
**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹80,000

Time (t) = 4 years

Simple Interest Increase = 40%

**Formula used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = P × r × t / 100

Amount (A) = P(1 + r/100)t

**Calculation:**

Simple Interest Increase = 40%

⇒ 40 = r × 4 / 100

⇒ r = 40 × 100 / 4

⇒ r = 10%

Now, find compound interest:

Amount (A) = P(1 + r/100)t

A = 80,000(1 + 10/100)⁴

⇒ A = 80,000(1 + 0.1)⁴

⇒ A = 80,000(1.1)⁴

⇒ A = 80,000 × 1.4641

⇒ A = ₹117,128

Compound Interest (CI) = A - P

CI = 117,128 - 80,000

⇒ CI = ₹37,128

**∴ The correct answer is option 2.**
